newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt issuance frenzy seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt issuance frenzy seen continuing.

text.p: Last week's new issue frenzy is expected to spill over into this week's business as attractive financing rates continue to lure issuers into the corporate debt arena, dealers said.
"The market still looks pretty healthy...today should set the tone for the rest of the week," said one high-grade syndicate source.
After last week's approximately $6.4 billion in new straight corporate debt issuance, more supply is seen as U.S. Treasury yields remain at their lowest levels since the spring, dealers said.
Currently, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading up 6/32 at 101-3/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
However, dealers noted that this week's U.S. Presidential election coupled with the Treasury's $38.5 billion quarterly refunding may lead to some volatility in the market.
"Market tone is very good right now; however, the elections tomorrow and the refunding this week may lead to volatility in the (Treasury) market," a syndicate source said.
But meanwhile opportunistic issuers continue to line up to bring new corporate debt to market capitalizing on the improved rate environment.
About $1.5 billion in new investment grade corporate debt is expected to hit the market this week, syndicate sources said.
Korea Development Bank is expected to price $500 million in A1/AA-minus 10-year debt, sources said.
Another $500 million is expected to come to market out of Husky Oil in a three-part debt offering via BT Securities.
The first tranche consist of $125 million in seven-year debt with price talk seen at 70 to 75 basis points.
The second tranche consist of $250 million in 10-year debt with price talk seen at 80 to 85 basis points.
The third tranche consist of $125 million in 20-year debt with price talk seen at 90 to 95 basis points.
Western Mining's $300 million in 10-year debt and Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co's $250 million debt offering are expected to come one day this week, syndicate sources said.
Turning to the high-yield sector, about $1.0 billion in private placement debt offerings are gearing up to come to market, dealers said.
YPF SA is expected to price $200 million in senior notes due 2001 via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Olympus Communications may price $200 million in 144A senior notes via Goldman Sachs & Co.
Parker Drilling is expected to issue $275 million in 144A senior notes due 2006 via Jeffries & Co.
Abraxas Petroleum is expected to issue $200 million in eight-year 144A notes via BT Securities. Price talk on the issue is seen at 10.75-11.0 percent, sources said.
Amtrol Inc may price $100 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006, sources added.
Pillowtex Corp may issue $125 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Nationsbanc Capital Markets.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
